1password.com.name: 1Password
1password.com.description: 1Password makes password and access management software for individuals, families and companies. It was founded in Toronto in 2005 by Dave Teare and Roustem Karimov and is still headquartered there, with David Faugno as chief executive. The company says more than 200,000 businesses use its products, and its business range now covers privileged access, device trust and the management of SaaS applications alongside the core password manager. It reports more than 1,400 employees and $400 million in annual recurring revenue.

a24films.com.name: A24
a24films.com.description: A24 is a New York studio that finances, produces and distributes feature films and makes television series. It was founded in 2012 by Daniel Katz, David Fenkel and John Hodges, and its films include Moonlight, Uncut Gems and Everything Everywhere All at Once. On television it has made Euphoria and Beef. The company also owns the Cherry Lane Theatre in New York, and a 2024 funding round led by Thrive Capital valued it at $3.5 billion.

acko.com.name: ACKO
acko.com.description: ACKO sells general and life insurance to Indian customers through its website and app, and also offers group health cover for employers. It was founded in Bengaluru in 2016, and the group runs Acko General Insurance and Acko Life Insurance under the holding company Acko Technology and Services. Its general insurance arm reported a net profit of ₹43.6 crore for FY26. The company has appointed bankers for a planned stock market listing, with a target of the first half of 2027.

acorns.com.name: Acorns
acorns.com.description: Acorns is a US consumer finance app for saving and investing small amounts over time. Alongside its round-up investing account, it offers an IRA retirement account called Later, Mighty Oak checking, an emergency savings account and Acorns Early for investing on behalf of children. The company was started by Walter and Jeff Cruttenden and is based in Irvine, California. It bought the children's money app GoHenry in 2023 and says it has served more than 16 million customers in total.

andela.com.name: Andela
andela.com.description: Andela recruits, vets and places software engineers and other technologists with employers, either as individual hires or as fully managed teams. It was founded in 2014 by a group that included Jeremy Johnson and Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, and Carrol Chang has been chief executive since September 2024. The company says its talent network reaches more than 135 countries and that it has served over 650 clients. Its newer services centre on AI engineering assessment, training and delivery, and it owns the coding challenge site Codewars, bought in 2023.

apna.co.name: apna
apna.co.description: apna runs a mobile app and website where job seekers in India look for work in roles such as field sales, accounts and telecalling, and where employers post vacancies and screen applicants. Nirmit Parikh launched it in December 2019, and a $100 million funding round in 2021 gave it unicorn status. The company says it connects more than 5.9 crore job seekers with about 7 lakh employers. For the year to March 2025 it reported operating revenue of ₹122 crore.

babbel.com.name: Babbel
babbel.com.description: Babbel sells subscription language courses through its app, along with podcasts, games and an AI conversation practice tool called Babbel Speak. The company traces its origins to 2007 and was founded by Markus Witte, Thomas Holl, Lorenz Heine and Toine Diepstraten. It has offices in Berlin and New York and says it has sold more than 30 million subscriptions. Its courses cover more than a dozen languages, among them Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Turkish, and its staff come from more than 80 nationalities.

btcmarkets.net.name: BTC Markets
btcmarkets.net.description: BTC Markets runs a cryptocurrency exchange for Australian customers, with trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Litecoin and other digital assets. It began operating in 2013 and works from Melbourne. The exchange serves individual traders, institutions and self-managed super funds, and added a mobile trading app in 2022. It reports more than 325,000 Australian traders and over AU$23 billion in total trade volume, and a sister company was granted an Australian Financial Services Licence in 2022.

bunq.com.name: bunq
bunq.com.description: bunq is an Amsterdam bank that runs entirely through its app and holds a European banking licence, which it received in September 2014. Ali Niknam founded the company in 2012 and still leads it as chief executive. The public app launched in November 2015 and the bank opened to customers across all EU markets in October 2019. It says it serves more than 22 million users, and it owns the group expense app tricount.

busuu.com.name: Busuu
busuu.com.description: Busuu was started in 2008 by Bernhard Niesner and Adrian Hilti, who met at IE Business School in Spain, and is based in London. Its courses cover about a dozen languages and mix short lessons, video clips and quizzes with AI speaking practice and corrections from native speakers. It reports over 120 million registered users and sells a corporate programme, Busuu for Business, to more than 600 organisations. The US education company Chegg bought Busuu for about US$436 million, with the deal completing in January 2022.

bybit.com.name: Bybit
bybit.com.description: Bybit operates a cryptocurrency exchange offering spot trading alongside perpetual contracts, futures and options. Ben Zhou founded it in 2018 in Singapore, and the company later moved its headquarters to Dubai. It says it has more than 80 million users worldwide. In the UAE it holds a full virtual asset platform operator licence from the Securities and Commodities Authority, and in October 2026 its Dubai entity received a VARA licence for spot exchange services.

cabify.com.name: Cabify
cabify.com.description: Cabify was founded in Madrid in 2011 by Juan de Antonio, who remains chief executive. It runs a ride-hailing app in more than 40 cities across Spain, Chile, Argentina, Peru, Colombia and Uruguay. Besides private rides it sells a corporate travel service for companies, a delivery and logistics arm and in-car advertising. The company reported revenue of about US$950 million for 2025.

calm.com.name: Calm
calm.com.description: Calm was started around 2012 by Michael Acton Smith and Alex Tew, and its app has passed 180 million downloads. Its library includes Sleep Stories, and it sells subscriptions monthly, yearly or as a one-off lifetime purchase. Calm Business supplies the app to employers, and Calm Health offers a clinical mental health programme through health plans and employers. The company works remote-first and hires staff across the UK and the US.

cambly.com.name: Cambly
cambly.com.description: Cambly was set up by Sameer Shariff and Kevin Law, two former Google employees, and went through the Y Combinator programme in San Francisco. Learners book video calls with English tutors on demand or follow structured courses in business English, grammar and exam preparation. Alongside one-to-one lessons it runs Cambly Kids for children, small group classes launched in 2022 and a corporate programme for companies. The platform takes students from more than 150 countries.

canonical.com.name: Canonical
canonical.com.description: Canonical was founded and funded in 2004 by Mark Shuttleworth to publish Ubuntu, the Linux distribution used on desktops, servers, cloud machines and devices. Revenue comes from Ubuntu Pro subscriptions, which add security maintenance and support, and from managed services for open source infrastructure such as OpenStack, Kubernetes, Ceph and databases. Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, released in April 2026, is the eleventh long-term supported version. The group is registered in London.

cardekho.com.name: CarDekho
cardekho.com.markets: India, plus Philippines, Malaysia and UAE through group sites
cardekho.com.description: CarDekho went live in 2008 and was started by Amit Jain and Anurag Jain in Jaipur. It is the main site of CarDekho Group, which also runs BikeDekho, ZigWheels, the vehicle loan platform Rupyy and car subscription brands Revv and Carrum, and holds a stake in InsuranceDekho. The group runs ZigWheels portals in the Philippines, Malaysia and the UAE. It reported consolidated operating revenue of ₹2,795 crore for FY25, and in July 2026 it was reported to be preparing draft papers for an Indian stock market listing.

careem.com.name: Careem
careem.com.description: Careem launched in Dubai in July 2012, founded by Mudassir Sheikha and Magnus Olsson, with Abdullah Elyas joining as a third co-founder in 2013. Its app combines ride-hailing with food ordering, Quik grocery delivery, the Careem Pay wallet and a Plus membership, and it says it has served more than 50 million customers. Uber bought Careem in 2019 and still owns the ride-hailing business, while the app and its other services sit in Careem Technologies. In June 2026 e& agreed to sell Uber a 12.5% stake in Careem Technologies, a deal that would give Uber control of that company.

carousell.com.name: Carousell
carousell.com.markets: Seven markets across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong
carousell.com.description: Carousell was launched in Singapore in August 2012 by Quek Siu Rui, Lucas Ngoo and Marcus Tan, who came up with the idea while studying at the National University of Singapore. The group now runs classifieds and resale businesses in seven markets, including Mudah.my in Malaysia, Cho Tot in Vietnam, the car platform OneShift, REFASH for second-hand fashion and Laku6 for used phones. It also operates physical resale stores in Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia and Indonesia. For FY25 it reported revenue of US$141 million and its first EBITDA profit.

cars24.com.name: CARS24
products: Car Info and Vehicle Info apps
cars24.com.description: CARS24 was founded in 2015 by Vikram Chopra, Mehul Agrawal, Ruchit Agarwal and Gajendra Jangid, and Chopra leads it as chief executive. It buys and sells used cars after inspection and adds loans, warranties and paperwork services such as registration transfers. Outside India it trades in Australia and the UAE. For FY26 it reported adjusted net revenue of ₹1,411 crore and ₹3,220 crore in loans disbursed, and its chief executive has said the company plans to list on Indian stock exchanges.

cashfree.com.name: Cashfree Payments
cashfree.com.markets: India, with cross-border collections and payouts
cashfree.com.description: Cashfree Payments was founded in 2015 by Akash Sinha and Reeju Datta and works from a headquarters in Bengaluru. It holds RBI authorisation as a payment aggregator for domestic and cross-border payments and as a prepaid payment instrument issuer. Its products cover online collections through more than 100 payment methods, bulk payouts, recurring payments, escrow and SecureID, a set of identity and KYC verification APIs. The company says it serves over one million businesses and processes about US$80 billion in transactions a year, and its investors include SBI, Apis Partners and KRAFTON.

casper.com.name: Casper
casper.com.description: Casper was founded in New York in 2014 by Philip Krim, Neil Parikh, Jeff Chapin, Gabe Flateman and Luke Sherwin, and began by selling a single mattress online. It listed on the New York Stock Exchange in early 2020 and was taken private by Durational Capital Management in 2022. In 2023 it sold its Canadian business to Sleep Country. Since late 2024 it has been a subsidiary of Carpenter Co., a polyurethane foam manufacturer based in Richmond, Virginia.

celonis.com.name: Celonis
celonis.com.description: Celonis was started in Munich in 2011 by a group of students including Alexander Rinke, now co-chief executive, and has dual headquarters in Munich and New York, with more than 20 offices in total. Its software reads event data from systems such as ERP and CRM tools to build a live model of how processes like order handling, invoicing and procurement actually run. The main product is the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform, which pairs process mining with AI, and the company added decision intelligence through its purchase of Ikigai Labs. It reports more than 3,000 employees.

darwinbox.com.name: Darwinbox
darwinbox.com.description: Darwinbox builds human capital management software for large employers, covering recruitment, onboarding, core HR, payroll, attendance, performance reviews and employee self-service on mobile. Chaitanya Peddi, Jayant Paleti and Rohit Chennamaneni founded it in Hyderabad in 2015. It now sells to more than 1,000 enterprises that together run about 4 million employees on the platform across 130 countries. Its backers include Partners Group, KKR, Salesforce Ventures and Teachers' Venture Growth, which invested US$40 million in 2025, and the platform supports the Model Context Protocol so AI agents can work with its HR data.

datacamp.com.name: DataCamp
datacamp.com.description: DataCamp teaches data science, AI and programming in the browser, with short video lessons followed by coding exercises that learners complete on the page. Courses cover Python, R, SQL and machine learning, and learners can follow career tracks, sit certifications or analyse data in DataLab, its AI-assisted notebook. The company says 21 million people have signed up, and it sells team plans to employers alongside a classroom programme for schools and universities. It was launched in Belgium by Jonathan Cornelissen, Dieter De Mesmaeker and Martijn Theuwissen and now has offices in New York, Leuven and London.

deel.com.name: Deel
deel.com.description: Deel lets companies hire, pay and manage staff in other countries without opening local entities, either by acting as employer of record or by handling contractor agreements and payroll for them. Alex Bouaziz and Shuo Wang started the company in 2019, and it says it now works with more than 40,000 businesses across 150 countries. Its range has grown to cover HR records, benefits, device management, immigration support and a US PEO service. A US$300 million Series E in October 2025 valued Deel at US$17.3 billion, and its own staff of over 4,000 work remotely from more than 100 countries.

degiro.com.name: DEGIRO
degiro.com.description: DEGIRO is an execution-only online broker for self-directed retail investors, giving access to around 50 exchanges in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific as well as over-the-counter trading. The German broker flatex bought the Dutch company in 2020, after regulators approved the deal that July, and DEGIRO now sits alongside the flatex and ViTrade brands within Frankfurt-based flatexDEGIRO SE. The group reported 3.66 million customer accounts across 16 European countries at the end of June 2026. DEGIRO customers can earn income from securities lending, and a wider savings plan offering is planned for late 2026.

depop.com.name: Depop
depop.com.description: Depop began in 2011 at the H-Farm incubator near Venice, where Simon Beckerman built the first version of the app, and moved its base to London in 2012. Sellers run shop profiles and list items with photos, and its audience is young, with nearly 90% of its roughly 7 million active buyers aged under 34 at the end of 2025. It also had more than 3 million active sellers and handles around US$1 billion in gross merchandise sales a year. Etsy bought Depop in 2021, and eBay acquired it from Etsy for about US$1.2 billion in July 2026, keeping the brand and app separate.
depop.com.status: Acquired by eBay from Etsy in July 2026

dhgate.com.name: DHgate
dhgate.com.description: DHgate runs a cross-border marketplace where Chinese manufacturers and traders sell goods in small wholesale lots or single units to buyers abroad, in categories from electronics and clothing to home goods. Diane Wang founded the business in Beijing in August 2004, and the website went live in 2005. It lists more than 34 million products from over 2.5 million registered suppliers and reports nearly 60 million registered buyers in 225 countries and regions. The company was reorganised as DHgate Group in 2022, and its app reached second place on the US App Store in April 2025.

discord.com.name: Discord
discord.com.description: Discord launched in May 2015 as a voice and text chat app for people playing games together, built by Jason Citron and Stanislav Vishnevskiy after running their own games studio. Users join invite-based servers organised into channels, and can hold group calls, stream their screens and play shared activities. The basic service is free, with revenue from the Nitro subscription, server boosts and sponsored Quests, and it reported more than 90 million daily active users in late 2025. Humam Sakhnini became chief executive in April 2025, and the company filed confidentially for a US listing in January 2026 but remains private.

docker.com.name: Docker
docker.com.description: Docker, Inc. sells the commercial tools built around Docker, the open source container technology that packages an application with its dependencies so it runs the same way on any machine. The company began as the platform-as-a-service provider dotCloud and took the Docker name in 2013, when founder Solomon Hykes refocused it on containers. Its main products are Docker Desktop for developers' computers, the Docker Hub image registry, Docker Scout and Docker Hardened Images for supply chain security, and newer tools for running AI agents and models. The Palo Alto company says more than 20 million developers use its software.

doctolib.fr.name: Doctolib
doctolib.fr.markets: France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the UK
doctolib.fr.description: Doctolib sells practice management and scheduling software to doctors, dentists and other health professionals, and runs a free website and app where patients book appointments and video consultations. Stanislas Niox-Chateau and a small team launched it in France in 2013, and it now operates in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. The company says it serves 520,000 health professionals and 90 million patients. In 2026 it entered the UK by buying Medicus, a supplier of GP electronic patient records, and Nvidia took a minority stake in October 2026 to support its AI work for clinicians and patients.

headspace.com.name: Headspace
headspace.com.description: Headspace began as a meditation app started in 2010 by Andy Puddicombe and Rich Pierson, and now combines guided meditation and sleep content with text-based coaching, licensed therapists and psychiatry. It merged with the teletherapy company Ginger in 2021, and much of its business comes from employers and health plans that offer it to staff and members, including as a replacement for a traditional employee assistance programme. The company says its app has been downloaded more than 105 million times. In September 2026 Headspace became part of Sword Health in an all-cash deal worth up to 300 million US dollars.
headspace.com.status: Acquired by Sword Health in September 2026

hmd.com.name: HMD
hmd.com.description: HMD, the trading name of HMD Global Oy, is a Finnish phone maker based in Espoo that took over the licence to sell Nokia-branded phones in 2016 after Microsoft left the phone business. It still sells phones under the Nokia licence alongside its own HMD-branded smartphones and feature phones, including repairable and family-focused models. A secure division makes devices such as the HMD Terra M for government and business users, and its Softlock platform lets retailers sell phones on credit with device-based locking. Jean-François Baril is chairman and chief executive.

hopper.com.name: Hopper
products: Price freeze and flexible booking add-ons
Travel booking technology for banks and partners
hopper.com.description: Hopper is a travel booking app whose main feature is price tracking that tells users whether to book now or wait. It was founded in Montreal in 2007 by former Expedia engineers including chief executive Frederic Lalonde and Joost Ouwerkerk, and spent several years building its price data before the app launched. Much of its revenue comes from booking commissions and paid add-ons such as price freezes and flexible cancellation. Hopper also licenses its booking technology to other companies, and RBC uses it to run the travel side of its Avion Rewards programme.

hostinger.com.name: Hostinger
hostinger.com.description: Hostinger sells web hosting, domains and website building tools to small businesses, freelancers and individuals. It started in Kaunas in 2004 as Hosting Media, a company bootstrapped by a group of young Lithuanian entrepreneurs, and is now based in Vilnius with more than 1,000 staff. Alongside shared, WordPress, VPS and cloud hosting, it offers an AI website builder, business email and a range of AI agent and automation tools such as self-hosted n8n. The company says more than five million businesses and creators in over 150 countries use its services.

hudabeauty.com.name: Huda Beauty
hudabeauty.com.description: Huda Beauty is a cosmetics brand started in Dubai in 2013 by the make-up artist and blogger Huda Kattan, whose first product was a range of false eyelashes. It now sells colour cosmetics and skincare through its own website and through retailers such as Sephora. TSG Consumer Partners held a minority stake from 2017 until June 2025, when Kattan bought back all outstanding shares and the brand returned to full independent ownership. Earlier in 2025 she sold her stake in the fragrance brand Kayali to her sister Mona Kattan, who runs it separately.

huel.com.name: Huel
huel.com.markets: UK, Europe and the United States
huel.com.description: Huel makes plant-based, nutritionally complete food, starting with powdered meals in 2015 and later adding ready-to-drink shakes, hot savoury meals, bars, greens powders and functional drinks. It sells mainly direct to consumers online, with a growing supermarket presence, and the UK is its largest market, followed by the United States and Europe. Revenue reached about £250 million in its tenth financial year. The French food group Danone agreed to buy the company in March 2026 and completed the acquisition in September 2026 after clearance from the UK Competition and Markets Authority.

idealista.com.name: idealista
products: Property listings for sale and rent
idealista.com.description: idealista runs online property portals in Spain, Italy and Portugal, where private owners and estate agents advertise homes, offices, garages and rooms for sale or rent. It was founded in Madrid in 2000 by the brothers Jesús and Fernando Encinar with César Oteiza, and Jesús Encinar remains chief executive. The private equity firm Cinven bought a majority stake from EQT in a deal valuing the company at about €2.9 billion, with founders and management keeping a share. Besides listings it sells software and data services to agents and has bought smaller businesses such as the overseas buyers' portal Kyero.

immobiliare.it.name: Immobiliare.it
products: Property listings for sale and rent
Software and services for estate agents
immobiliare.it.description: Immobiliare.it runs one of Italy's main property listing sites, where estate agents, builders and private owners advertise homes and commercial premises for sale or rent. It was set up in 2005 by Silvio Pagliani and Andrea Piccioni, and Pagliani took over as chief executive in 2022. The company works from offices in Rome and Milan and heads a group of property portals in other countries, including Spitogatos in Greece, Immotop in Luxembourg, Nepremicnine.net in Slovenia and Indomio in Spain and the Balkans. It also runs the international site LuxuryEstate.com.

impossiblefoods.com.name: Impossible Foods
impossiblefoods.com.markets: United States, Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau and UAE
impossiblefoods.com.description: Impossible Foods makes plant-based versions of beef, chicken and pork, sold in supermarkets and to restaurants. It grew out of work begun in 2009 by the Stanford biochemist Pat Brown and is based in Redwood City, California. Its best known product is the Impossible Burger, launched in 2016, which uses soy leghemoglobin, a protein made by fermentation, to give a meat-like flavour and colour. The products are sold in nine markets including the United States, Canada, the UK, Australia and Singapore. Since chief executive Peter McGuinness left in January 2026, a three-person executive team has run the company.

independentreserve.com.name: Independent Reserve
independentreserve.com.description: Independent Reserve is a Sydney-based cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2013 by Adrian Przelozny, Adam Tepper and Lasanka Perera. It lets individuals, companies, trusts and self-managed super funds buy and sell crypto in Australian, New Zealand and other currencies, and runs an OTC desk for larger trades. In Australia it is registered with AUSTRAC as a digital currency exchange, and in 2021 it became the first Australian exchange to receive a Major Payment Institution licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The company says it has more than 550,000 clients.

indrive.com.name: inDrive
indrive.com.markets: Latin America, Africa, Asia and other regions, about 1,100 cities
indrive.com.description: inDrive runs a ride-hailing app built around fare negotiation, in which passengers name a price and nearby drivers accept it or make a counter-offer. Arsen Tomsky started the service in Yakutsk, Siberia, in 2013 and remains chief executive. It works mainly in Latin America, Africa, South and Central Asia and Southeast Asia, with Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia and Pakistan among its largest markets, and it says the app has been downloaded 400 million times. Besides city and intercity rides it offers courier deliveries and a financial services line called inDrive.Money, and employs close to 3,000 people across 28 offices.

instructure.com.name: Instructure
instructure.com.description: Instructure develops Canvas, a learning management system that schools, universities and employers use to run courses, set assignments and track grades online. The company was founded in 2008 and is based in Salt Lake City, Utah, with further offices in London and Quezon City. It also owns Mastery Connect for school assessment and Parchment, a service for sending academic transcripts and credentials. Instructure was listed on the New York Stock Exchange until November 2024, when the investment firm KKR, with Dragoneer, completed a 4.8 billion US dollar purchase and took it private. It says its tools reach about 200 million learners.
instructure.com.status: Active (taken private by KKR in November 2024)

internshala.com.name: Internshala
internshala.com.description: Internshala began in 2010 as a blog run by IIT Madras graduate Sarvesh Agrawal and launched its website in 2013, later adding an Android app in 2015. Based in Gurugram, it lists internships and fresher jobs posted by employers, and sells short online trainings and placement courses in subjects such as digital marketing, data science and full stack development. It reports more than 34 million registered users and around 450,000 employers. In February 2026 the edtech company upGrad agreed to acquire it in a mostly stock-swap deal, with Internshala kept as a separate brand under Agrawal.
internshala.com.status: Acquired by upGrad in 2026, operating as a separate brand

italki.com.name: italki
italki.com.description: italki is a marketplace where people book private video lessons with language teachers who set their own prices and timetables. It was founded in 2007 by Kevin Chen and Yongyue Jiang, is registered in Hong Kong as italki HK Limited, and has run its development work from Shanghai. Learners choose between professional teachers and community tutors, and pay per lesson or in packages. The site says it lists more than 20,000 teachers covering over 150 languages, with learners from more than 190 countries, and it also offers language level assessments.

iyzico.com.name: iyzico
iyzico.com.description: iyzico was founded in Istanbul in 2012 by Barbaros Özbugutu and Tahsin Işın and handles online and in-store card payments for Turkish businesses, from small sellers to marketplaces. Its merchant products include a virtual POS, payment links, subscriptions, mass payouts and fraud controls, while shoppers use the iyzico app and Pay with iyzico to store cards and pay. PayU, part of Prosus, bought the company in 2019, and in 2025 iyzico completed its purchase of the payments firm Paynet. It reports 185,000 merchant members and 7 million wallet users, and in March 2026 announced a move into Europe through a Dutch subsidiary.

joinhandshake.com.name: Handshake
joinhandshake.com.description: Handshake runs a careers network that links university students and recent graduates with employers, working through university career centres that give their students access. Garrett Lord, Ben Christensen and Scott Ringwelski started the company in 2014, and it says more than 1,600 educational institutions and about one million employers now use it. It has also set up Handshake AI, which recruits people with specialist knowledge for AI training and evaluation work. The company has offices in San Francisco, New York, the UK and Bangalore.

luno.com.name: Luno
products: Crypto buying, selling and storage app
Crypto as a service for partners
luno.com.description: Luno runs a crypto investment app and exchange that started in South Africa in 2013 under the name BitX and is now headquartered in London. Digital Currency Group, the US crypto investment firm, bought the whole company in September 2020. Besides retail trading and staking, Luno offers white-label crypto services for partners, an over-the-counter desk with a cross-border settlement network, and Zaru, a rand-backed stablecoin launched in February 2026. In mid-2026 it narrowed its focus to core markets in Africa and South East Asia and stopped serving some other regions from 1 September 2026.

magoosh.com.name: Magoosh
magoosh.com.description: Magoosh was started in 2009 by students at the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley, and the company is still based in Berkeley, although it has worked fully remotely since March 2020. Its self-paced courses cover the GRE, GMAT, LSAT, MCAT, SAT, ACT, TOEFL, IELTS and Praxis, combining short video lessons with practice questions. Magoosh says more than 10 million students have used its material, with learners in 185 countries. It also sells test prep packages to high schools and colleges, and co-founder Bhavin Parikh is chief executive.

malt.com.name: Malt
malt.com.markets: Nine countries and regions in Europe and the Middle East
malt.com.description: Malt began in France in 2013 under the name Hopwork and took its current name as it expanded into other European countries. Companies use the platform to find, contract and pay freelance developers, designers, marketers, data specialists and consultants, with Malt handling the paperwork and payments between the two sides. In June 2026 it reported more than one million registered freelancers and over 100,000 client businesses, and said business volume on the platform passed 800 million euros in 2024. Its head office is in Paris, and clients it names include Schneider Electric, L'Oréal and Reckitt.

masterclass.com.name: MasterClass
masterclass.com.description: MasterClass launched in San Francisco in May 2015 with online classes recorded by well-known practitioners, from chefs and novelists to athletes and business founders. An annual membership gives unlimited access to a library of more than 200 instructors and classes. The company has since added MasterClass at Work, which sells training to employers, MasterClass On Call, which offers AI roleplays and real-time coaching, and certificate programmes developed with companies. Co-founder Aaron Rasmussen was the company's first chief technology officer and creative director.

medium.com.name: Medium
medium.com.description: Medium was launched in August 2012 by Twitter co-founder Evan Williams as a place where anyone could publish long-form writing. The site sells no advertising and is paid for by reader memberships, part of which goes to writers whose stories members read. Medium says more than 100 million people use it each month, and many companies, editors and writers run their own publications on it. Tony Stubblebine took over from Williams as chief executive in 2022.

memrise.com.name: Memrise
memrise.com.description: Memrise was founded in London in 2010 by memory champion Ed Cooke, Ben Whately and neuroscientist Greg Detre, and began as a vocabulary tool built on spaced repetition. The app now mixes word drills with short videos of native speakers, AI conversation practice, pronunciation tools and exam preparation for IELTS, GCSE, A-Level and IB with AI marking. The company says it has had more than 80 million learners in 189 countries and offers courses in 149 languages. It runs with a small team of around a dozen people.

mercadobitcoin.com.br.name: Mercado Bitcoin
mercadobitcoin.com.br.description: Mercado Bitcoin has run a cryptocurrency exchange in Brazil since 2013, letting customers buy and sell bitcoin, stablecoins and other digital assets in reais. It belongs to the holding company 2TM, whose chief executive Roberto Dagnoni also chairs and runs the exchange. In 2023 the Central Bank of Brazil authorised the group to operate as a payment institution issuing electronic money, which backs its MB Pay digital account. By July 2026 the platform had about 4.5 million users and had taken a R$100 million investment from Tether to expand into payments and tokenised investments.
mercadobitcoin.com.br.status: Active; deposits and withdrawals were paused from 2 November 2026 after a security incident

mercury.com.name: Mercury
products: Working capital loans and venture debt
mercury.com.description: Mercury was set up in San Francisco in 2017 by three former colleagues from the ad network Heyzap and opened its first accounts in 2019. It is a financial technology company rather than a bank, and its deposit accounts are held at partner banks Choice Financial Group and Column N.A. Beyond checking and savings it offers cards, bill pay, invoicing, payroll, accounting software and lending, and says it serves more than 300,000 businesses. In April 2026 it won conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to form Mercury Bank, N.A., which will be based in Utah.

mollie.com.name: Mollie
mollie.com.description: Mollie was started in Amsterdam in 2004 by Adriaan Mol and grew into a payments provider for European businesses of all sizes, from web shops to software platforms that embed payments. Mollie B.V. is licensed as an electronic money institution by De Nederlandsche Bank, and Mollie UK Ltd is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority. Alongside card and local payment methods it offers in-person terminals, recurring billing, business accounts and merchant financing. In September 2026 it completed its purchase of the UK direct debit company GoCardless, and the combined group serves more than 350,000 businesses in over 30 markets under chief executive Koen Köppen.

patreon.com.name: Patreon
patreon.com.description: Patreon was started in 2013 by musician Jack Conte and Sam Yam and is based in San Francisco. Artists, podcasters, video makers and writers use it to charge fans a monthly fee for access to their work, and can also offer free memberships. The company says more than 300,000 creators use the platform and that creators have earned over $10 billion through it since launch. More than 10 million fans pay for memberships each month.

paystack.com.name: Paystack
paystack.com.markets: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Côte d'Ivoire
paystack.com.description: Paystack launched in Nigeria in 2016 and was the first Nigerian startup accepted into Y Combinator. Stripe bought the Lagos company in 2020 in a deal reported at over $200 million. It now serves around 300,000 merchants across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Côte d'Ivoire. In 2026 it announced The Stack Group, a holding company for Paystack, the Zap consumer transfer app and Paystack Microfinance Bank, subject to regulatory approval.

pedidosya.com.name: PedidosYa
pedidosya.com.description: PedidosYa was founded in Montevideo in 2009 by Ariel Burschtin, Álvaro García and Ruben Sosenke, and Delivery Hero bought it in 2014. Its app takes orders for restaurant meals, groceries and other goods and delivers them through its rider network. It runs in Uruguay, Argentina, Peru, Paraguay, Bolivia and several Central American and Caribbean countries. In 2026 Uber launched a takeover offer for Delivery Hero, with settlement expected in the second half of 2027.

peopleperhour.com.name: PeoplePerHour
peopleperhour.com.description: PeoplePerHour went live in September 2007, set up by engineers Xenios Thrasyvoulou and Simos Kitiris with a focus on UK small businesses. Clients can post a project and receive proposals, or buy fixed-price service offers listed by freelancers, and pay by the hour or by the job. The company describes itself as founder owned and led. It says it has connected more than a million clients and freelancers and paid out over £100 million to freelancers.

pepperfry.com.name: Pepperfry
pepperfry.com.description: Pepperfry was set up in Mumbai in 2011 by former eBay executives Ambareesh Murty and Ashish Shah, and its website went live in January 2012. It sells furniture and home goods online and through a network of more than 100 offline studios. BSE-listed TCC Concept Limited completed its acquisition of a majority stake in December 2025. Pepperfry reported its first profitable quarter in the fourth quarter of FY26.
pepperfry.com.status: Active; acquired by TCC Concept Limited in December 2025

personio.com.name: Personio
personio.com.description: Personio was founded in Munich in 2015 by Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher, Arseniy Vershinin and Ignaz Forstmeier, and Renner is chief executive. It sells HR and payroll software aimed at organisations with roughly 25 to 5,000 staff. More than 16,000 companies and 1.6 million people use it, and it employs over 1,500 people across six European offices. In 2026 it bought the recruiting AI startup Aurio and the Berlin spend management company Circula, and became a certified B Corp.

pharmeasy.in.name: PharmEasy
pharmeasy.in.description: PharmEasy started in Mumbai in 2015 and is run by API Holdings, the group that also holds a controlling stake in the listed diagnostics firm Thyrocare. Customers use its app and website to order prescription medicines, over-the-counter and wellness products for home delivery, and to book lab tests. Rahul Guha became chief executive in August 2025, when co-founder Siddharth Shah moved to vice-chairman of API Holdings. The group has said an IPO or a merger with Thyrocare remain options once it reaches its profitability target.

plaid.com.name: Plaid
plaid.com.markets: United States, United Kingdom and EU
plaid.com.description: Plaid was founded in 2013 by Zach Perret and William Hockey, and Perret is chief executive. It runs the connections that let finance apps link to a person's bank account to verify it, move money or read balances and transactions with permission. The company says more than 9,000 fintechs build on Plaid and that it supports over 12,000 financial institutions. A share sale in February 2026 was reported to value it at about $8 billion.

pluralsight.com.name: Pluralsight
pluralsight.com.description: Pluralsight was founded in Utah in 2004 by Aaron Skonnard, Fritz Onion, Keith Brown and Bill Williams, and grew for about nine years without outside funding. It sells technology training to individuals and businesses, with more than 6,500 courses, skill assessments and hands-on labs covering software, cloud, AI and security. The company says over 23,000 organisations use it. Vista Equity Partners bought it in 2021, a lender group led by Blue Owl took control in 2024, and it set up a new headquarters in Westlake, Texas in 2025.
pluralsight.com.status: Active; owned by a lender group led by Blue Owl Capital since 2024

poshmark.com.name: Poshmark
poshmark.com.description: Poshmark was founded in 2011 by Manish Chandra, Chetan Pungaliya, Gautam Golwala and Tracy Sun and is based in Redwood City, California. Sellers list clothing, shoes, accessories and home items from a phone, and buyers can also shop through live selling shows. The company says it has over 130 million members in the US and Canada and that more than 350 million items have sold. South Korea's Naver bought it for $1.2 billion in January 2023, and Naver executive Namsun Kim became chief executive in October 2025.
poshmark.com.status: Active; acquired by Naver in January 2023

practo.com.name: Practo
practo.com.markets: India, the US and the UAE
practo.com.description: Practo was founded in 2008 by Shashank ND and Abhinav Lal and is based in Bengaluru. Patients use its app to find doctors, book clinic visits, consult online and order lab tests and medicines, while clinics and hospitals use its Ray and Insta software to run their practices. It has expanded from India into the US and the UAE. Jagnoor Singh is chief executive and Shashank ND is executive chairman, and a public listing has been reported as planned for 2027.

prodigygame.com.name: Prodigy Education
prodigygame.com.description: Prodigy Education began in 2011 as an undergraduate project by Alex Peters and Rohan Mahimker, who still lead the company as co-chief executives. Its games put elementary school pupils on quests in a fantasy world where progress depends on answering curriculum-aligned questions. Teachers can use Prodigy Math free of charge, and the company earns money from optional paid memberships for families. It has raised funding from TPG Growth and the Canadian Business Growth Fund.

propertyfinder.ae.name: Property Finder
products: Property listings for sale and rent
propertyfinder.ae.description: Property Finder was founded in Dubai in 2007 by Michael Lahyani, who remains chief executive. Its website and app list homes and commercial property for sale and rent from agents and developers in the UAE and other Middle East and North Africa markets. It also offers a home valuation tool and a credit score service for buyers. In January 2026 it raised $170 million in a round led by Mubadala, after a $525 million investment led by Permira in 2025.

propertyguru.com.sg.name: PropertyGuru
propertyguru.com.sg.ownership: Subsidiary of EQT Private Capital Asia
propertyguru.com.sg.description: PropertyGuru started in Singapore in 2007 and now runs property listing sites across four Southeast Asian countries. Its brands include PropertyGuru in Singapore and Malaysia, iProperty in Malaysia, DDproperty in Thailand and Batdongsan in Vietnam, alongside tools for agents and the Asia Property Awards. EQT Private Capital Asia bought the group for about $1.1 billion in December 2024 and took it off the New York Stock Exchange. Lewis Ng has been chief executive since March 2025, and the group had more than 1,200 staff at the end of 2025.
propertyguru.com.sg.status: Active; taken private by EQT in December 2024

proton.me.name: Proton
proton.me.description: Proton was started in Geneva in 2014 by scientists who met at CERN, and co-founder Andy Yen is chief executive. It began with the encrypted email service Proton Mail and has added a VPN, cloud storage, a password manager, calendar, documents and an AI assistant called Lumo. The company passed 100 million registered users in early 2026. Since 2024 its main shareholder has been the non-profit Proton Foundation, and it has no venture capital investors.

public.com.name: Public
public.com.description: Public is a New York brokerage run by co-founders and co-chief executives Leif Abraham and Jannick Malling. Its app and website let US customers trade stocks, ETFs, options and crypto, buy corporate bonds and Treasuries, and hold cash and retirement accounts. The broker-dealer, Open to the Public Investing, is a FINRA member, and Public Advisors is an SEC-registered investment adviser. It promotes AI tools that summarise earnings calls and can act on a customer's instructions.

purplle.com.name: Purplle
purplle.com.description: Purplle was founded in Mumbai in 2012 by Manish Taneja, Rahul Dash and Suyash Katyayani, and the business is run by Manash Lifestyle Private Limited. It sells makeup, skincare, haircare and body care from Indian and international brands through its app and website, alongside beauty brands it owns. The company has raised about $480 million across several funding rounds, most recently in October 2024.

qonto.com.name: Qonto
qonto.com.markets: France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria, Belgium, Portugal and the Netherlands
qonto.com.description: Qonto was founded in Paris in 2017 by Alexandre Prot and Steve Anavi. It provides online business accounts, payment cards, invoicing and bookkeeping tools to small companies and freelancers in eight European countries. Qonto SA holds a payment institution licence from the French regulator ACPR, granted in 2018. The company says it has more than 750,000 customers and about 1,700 employees.

ridedott.com.name: Dott
ridedott.com.markets: 20 countries in Europe and the Middle East
ridedott.com.description: Dott rents shared electric scooters and e-bikes by the minute through its app in cities across Europe and the Middle East. Henri Moissinac and Maxim Romain founded it in Amsterdam in 2018, and in 2024 it merged with Berlin-based TIER Mobility, after which TIER riders and vehicles moved over to the Dott app and brand. The combined company reported about 200,000 vehicles in 400 cities and 20 countries, with 76.9 million rides and €173.3 million in net revenue in 2025. Maxim Romain is chief executive and Henri Moissinac is executive chairman.

sharechat.com.name: ShareChat
sharechat.com.description: ShareChat is built by Mohalla Tech, a Bengaluru company that launched the app in October 2015 for people who prefer to post and browse in Indian languages rather than English. The app works in 14 languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Bhojpuri and Haryanvi. Mohalla Tech also runs the Moj short-video app and QuickTV, a subscription service for short serial dramas. Revenue for the 2025-26 financial year rose about 40% to roughly Rs 1,016 crore, and the company has said it is preparing for a stock market listing.

shiprocket.in.name: Shiprocket
shiprocket.in.markets: India, with international shipping to 220+ countries and territories
shiprocket.in.description: Shiprocket started in 2017 as a shipping tool for small online sellers and now runs a wider set of services from its Gurugram corporate office, including warehousing and fulfilment, cross-border shipping, a one-click checkout called Fastrr and working-capital lending. It says it serves more than 2.5 lakh online retailers and reaches over 19,000 Indian pin codes through 17-plus courier partners. The company listed its shares on the NSE and BSE on 19 August 2026, debuting at about 35% above its Rs 97 issue price.
shiprocket.in.status: Active. Listed on NSE and BSE in August 2026

simplilearn.com.name: Simplilearn
simplilearn.com.description: Simplilearn sells online courses and longer programmes in areas such as data science, AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity, project management and digital marketing, many of them run with universities including Purdue, Caltech CTME and UMass Amherst, and with Indian institutes such as IIT Roorkee and IIM Indore. Courses mix recorded material with live online classes. Founded in Bengaluru in 2010, it also has offices in Plano, Texas and Singapore. Blackstone bought a controlling stake in 2021 for $250 million, and the company now describes itself as a Blackstone company.

siteground.com.name: SiteGround
siteground.com.description: SiteGround was started in 2004 by a group of university friends in Sofia and has stayed privately owned, with no outside shareholders. It runs its service from data centres in the United States, Europe, Singapore and Australia, and says it manages more than three million domains. Alongside hosting it has built its own tools, including a site builder, an AI website and web app builder called Coderick AI, and a standalone email marketing service. The group has companies registered in the USA, UK, Spain, Cyprus and Bulgaria and more than 500 staff.

skillshare.com.name: Skillshare
skillshare.com.description: Skillshare runs a subscription library of short video classes taught by working creatives, covering subjects such as illustration, graphic design, photography, video, writing and freelancing. Most classes end with a hands-on project that students post for others to see. Anyone can apply to teach, and teachers are paid from the subscription revenue. The company was founded in New York in November 2010 and first ran in-person local classes before moving fully to online video.

skyscanner.net.name: Skyscanner
skyscanner.net.description: Skyscanner grew out of a spreadsheet of flight prices that three friends built in Edinburgh, and the company was formed in 2003. It does not sell tickets itself. Searches return fares and rates from more than 1,200 airlines, travel agents, hotel sites and rental firms, and the user books with the chosen provider. The company says more than 100 million people use its website and app each month. China's Ctrip, now Trip.com Group, bought Skyscanner in 2016 for about $1.75 billion, and it keeps offices in Edinburgh, Barcelona, Miami and Singapore.

snapdeal.com.name: Snapdeal
snapdeal.com.description: Snapdeal was founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal and now concentrates on lower-priced fashion, home and lifestyle goods for shoppers in smaller towns and cities. In the 2025-26 financial year it delivered to 18,972 pin codes. The marketplace belongs to AceVector, the renamed group company that also owns the Unicommerce e-commerce software business and Stellaro Brands, a consumer brands unit. AceVector listed on the NSE and BSE in October 2026.
snapdeal.com.status: Active. Parent AceVector listed on NSE and BSE in October 2026

soundcloud.com.name: SoundCloud
products: SoundCloud Go and Go+ listener plans
soundcloud.com.description: SoundCloud was founded in Berlin in 2007 by Swedish sound designer Alexander Ljung and musician Eric Wahlforss as a place for musicians to share recordings. Anyone can upload, and the company says more than 40 million creators use it, which gives it a large catalogue of remixes, DJ sets and early releases. Listeners can stream free with ads or pay for Go or Go+, while artists can buy a subscription that bundles distribution to other services. Eliah Seton has been chief executive since 2023, and in July 2026 the company bought the independent music platform Nina Protocol.

squarespace.com.name: Squarespace
squarespace.com.description: Squarespace sells subscription software for building and running websites, with design templates, an AI site builder, domain registration, online stores, invoicing and email marketing in one account. It also owns Acuity Scheduling, an appointment booking tool. Anthony Casalena started the company in his university dorm room at the University of Maryland in 2003 and still runs it. Investment firm Permira took Squarespace private in October 2024 in a deal worth about $7.2 billion, ending its listing on the New York Stock Exchange. It has offices in New York, Dublin and Aveiro in Portugal.
squarespace.com.status: Active. Taken private by Permira in October 2024

squareyards.com.name: Square Yards
squareyards.com.description: Square Yards was set up in Gurugram in 2014 by Tanuj Shori and Kanika Gupta Shori and earns most of its money from brokering new and resale homes. Over time it has added Urban Money for mortgages, Azuro for rentals and property management, Interior Company for home interiors, and PropVR for 3D and virtual reality tours. India produced 88% of revenue in the 2025-26 financial year, with the rest from the UAE, Australia and Canada. Group revenue that year was about Rs 2,086 crore, and the company has hired banks for a planned stock market listing.

upgrad.com.name: upGrad
upgrad.com.description: upGrad sells online degrees, postgraduate diplomas and certificate courses run with universities in India and abroad, alongside study abroad programmes and corporate training through upGrad Enterprise. It was started in Mumbai in 2015 by Ronnie Screwvala, Mayank Kumar, Phalgun Kompalli and Ravijot Chugh. In FY26 it reported gross revenue of about Rs 2,070 crore and more than 100,000 learners enrolled at any one time. The company has agreed to acquire Internshala and Unacademy, and Screwvala has said it intends to list on the stock market in 2027.

upstox.com.name: Upstox
upstox.com.description: Upstox runs a trading and investing app for Indian retail investors, covering equities, futures and options, commodities, IPOs, mutual funds and fixed deposits. The broking business operates as Upstox Securities Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of RKSV Securities India, and was co-founded by Ravi Kumar, Kavitha Subramanian and Shrini Viswanath. The company says it has more than 2 crore customers. Tiger Global is among its investors, and in August 2026 the company was reported to be in talks with bankers about a public listing.

urbanladder.com.name: Urban Ladder
urbanladder.com.description: Urban Ladder started in Bengaluru in 2012 selling furniture online and later opened its own stores in several Indian cities. Its range covers sofas, beds, dining and study furniture, storage, mattresses and home decor such as lighting, rugs and wall art. Reliance Retail bought a 96 per cent stake in 2020 for about Rs 182 crore, and the website now names Reliance Retail Limited as the operating entity. The company was founded by Ashish Goel and Rajiv Srivatsa.

vedantu.com.name: Vedantu
products: Live online classes for school students
vedantu.com.description: Vedantu was set up in 2014 by Vamsi Krishna, Pulkit Jain and Anand Prakash and is based in Bengaluru. It teaches school students up to Class 12 through live online classes and runs coaching for JEE and NEET, along with crash courses for exams such as CUET and NDA. It also runs offline and hybrid learning centres, and in 2022 it bought the Karnataka coaching chain Deeksha, which now trades as Deeksha Vedantu. The company reported a profitable fourth quarter in FY25 after several years of cost cutting.

vercel.com.name: Vercel
vercel.com.description: Vercel provides a cloud platform where developers deploy websites and web apps, with hosting, a global content delivery network, serverless compute and observability tools built in. Guillermo Rauch founded the company in 2015, and it maintains the open-source Next.js framework, which recorded more than 500 million downloads in the year to September 2025. Newer products include v0, which generates app code from text prompts, and the AI SDK for adding AI features to applications. In September 2025 Vercel raised a $300 million Series F co-led by Accel and GIC at a $9.3 billion valuation.

vinted.com.name: Vinted
vinted.com.description: Vinted runs an online marketplace and app where people sell and buy secondhand clothes, shoes, accessories, children's items and homeware. It was founded in Vilnius in 2008 by Justas Janauskas and Milda Mitkutė and is now available in 26 countries, mostly in Europe, after launching in Latvia, Estonia and Slovenia in 2025. The wider Vinted Group also runs Vinted Go, a parcel delivery network, and Vinted Pay for payments. In 2025 the group reported revenue of €1.1 billion, up 38 per cent, on €10.8 billion of gross merchandise value.

voi.com.name: Voi
voi.com.description: Voi rents shared electric scooters and e-bikes that riders find and unlock through its app. It was founded in Stockholm in 2018 and now runs more than 200,000 vehicles in over 130 towns and cities across 13 countries, with around 1,000 staff. Riders have taken more than 500 million trips on Voi vehicles since launch, and the company counts over 4 million active riders a year. In the third quarter of 2026 it reported net revenue of €88.2 million, up 53 per cent on a year earlier.

vultr.com.name: Vultr
vultr.com.description: Vultr sells cloud infrastructure to developers and businesses, including virtual machines, bare metal servers, cloud GPUs, managed Kubernetes, load balancers and block and object storage. David Aninowsky founded the company in 2014, and it was self-funded for more than a decade before taking outside investment. It runs 32 cloud data centre regions and has customers in 185 countries. In December 2024 it raised equity from LuminArx and AMD Ventures at a $3.5 billion valuation, followed by $329 million in credit financing in June 2025 to expand its AI capacity.

wallapop.com.name: Wallapop
wallapop.com.description: Wallapop runs a marketplace app where individuals buy and sell used goods, either collecting nearby or having items shipped. It was founded in Barcelona in 2013, where it is still based, and expanded into Italy in 2021 and Portugal in 2022. The platform has more than 19 million monthly active users. South Korea's NAVER, which already held 29.5 per cent, agreed in August 2025 to buy the remaining 70.5 per cent for €377 million, and the acquisition completed in January 2026.

wealthsimple.com.name: Wealthsimple
products: Self-directed trading in stocks, ETFs and options
wealthsimple.com.description: Wealthsimple offers Canadians self-directed trading in stocks, ETFs, options and crypto, managed portfolios, registered accounts such as TFSAs and RRSPs, chequing and savings, a credit card, mortgages and tax filing software. It was founded in Toronto in 2014 and is led by co-founder and chief executive Michael Katchen. The company reported C$169.2 billion in assets under administration at the end of September 2026 and more than 4 million clients. In October 2026 it announced a funding round of up to C$425 million led by GIC at a C$13.8 billion valuation.

webflow.com.name: Webflow
webflow.com.description: Webflow makes a browser-based visual tool for designing, building and hosting websites, with a content management system, ecommerce, localisation and SEO features in the same product. Vlad and Sergie Magdalin co-founded it in 2013, and the company is based in San Francisco with staff working in 18 countries. It says more than 300,000 organisations use the platform. Webflow has raised $335 million from investors including Accel and CapitalG, and in March 2026 it acquired Vidoso.ai as it added AI agent tools for marketing teams.

wellfound.com.name: Wellfound
wellfound.com.description: Wellfound runs a hiring platform for startups, where companies post jobs for free and candidates apply to roles at early-stage and growing technology firms, many of them remote. It began as AngelList Talent inside AngelList and was spun out as a separate company under the Wellfound name in November 2022, trading through AL Talent, Inc. Paid products include Reach, which uses AI to source candidates, and Autopilot, a managed recruiting service. The company says more than 10 million candidates have opted in and over 27,000 companies are hiring on the site.

wework.com.name: WeWork
wework.com.description: WeWork leases flexible workspace, from hot desks and dedicated desks to private offices, full floors and meeting rooms, with memberships such as All Access and On Demand for people who move between sites. Its website lists around 600 locations in more than 100 cities. The company filed for Chapter 11 in November 2023 and emerged in June 2024 as a private company with Yardi Systems as its majority owner. It is led by chief executive John Santora, a former Cushman & Wakefield executive.
wework.com.status: Active (emerged from Chapter 11 in June 2024, now privately owned)

withings.com.name: Withings
products: Smart scales with body composition and ECG
Withings Health Solutions remote patient monitoring
withings.com.description: Withings designs connected health devices for home use, including scales that measure body composition and ECG, hybrid smartwatches, blood pressure monitors and sleep trackers that sync to its app. Eric Carreel co-founded the French company in 2008, sold it to Nokia in 2016 and bought it back in 2018. About two thirds of its 2025 revenue came from FDA-cleared medical devices, and it reports 15 million active users with a team of around 400. Its Withings Health Solutions arm supplies remote patient monitoring to healthcare providers, and the United States is its largest market.

wolt.com.name: Wolt
wolt.com.description: Wolt runs a delivery app for ordering from restaurants, grocery shops and other retailers, and it also operates its own Wolt Market grocery stores, the Wolt+ subscription and Wolt Drive, a delivery service for other businesses. Six co-founders started the company in Helsinki in 2014, and it now works in more than 30 countries and over 1,000 cities. DoorDash completed its acquisition of Wolt in May 2022. The company says it has more than 15,000 employees and over 290,000 courier partners.
